title: Custom validators, asynchronous validation and error messages

videos.script:
The form from lesson fourteen sends an empty date to the server and lets the server refuse it. This lesson makes the form know first, and say so where a person will find it.

{{builtin}} You start with the validators Angular ships: required, min and max. Each failure leaves its own key in the control's errors.

{{messages}} Then the messages. A field's message appears once the field has been left, sits under it, and is tied to it so a screen reader reads both. On submit, the focus goes to the first problem.

{{custom}} You write two validators of your own: one for a day that has already gone, and one for two dates that are the same.

{{async}} An asynchronous validator asks the server whether the day is free, and the form waits while it is pending.

{{server}} And the server checks everything again, because the form is not the only way in.
